profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This is a Tata Communications cable landing station facility in Hillsboro, Oregon. Tata Communications is a global telecommunications and network services provider headquartered in Mumbai, India, a subsidiary of the Tata Group, operating one of the world's largest wholly owned subsea cable networks, marketed as the Tata Global Network, spanning roughly 500,000 route kilometers and connecting more than 190 countries. In the United States, Tata Communications operates cable landing stations terminating segments of this network, including this Hillsboro, Oregon facility and the Wall Township, New Jersey landing station, also recorded separately in this registry under a duplicate Tata operator record. Tata Communications should be distinguished from its former data center and colocation joint venture business: in 2021 ST Telemedia Global Data Centres acquired Tata Communications' remaining stake in their jointly held Singapore data center business, meaning branded colocation facilities that once carried the Tata Communications name there moved to STT GDC ownership; the submarine cable network and US landing stations were not part of that transaction. No published critical IT megawatt figures were found for this landing station. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

reading.body:
TGN Hillsboro is a submarine cable landing station operated by Tata Communications, a global telecommunications company that owns one of the world's largest wholly owned subsea cable networks spanning roughly 500,000 route kilometers. The facility terminates segments of this network at a location in the Portland metropolitan area. No critical IT megawatt capacity is published for this site.

Without published power figures, this facility cannot be ranked among Oregon's published data center capacity, though it is mapped as one of 133 facilities in the state. Oregon has published specifications for only eight of its mapped facilities totaling 156.6 MW, and this campus does not appear in that subset.

Cable landing stations are infrastructure for international connectivity rather than AI compute hosting. The functions this site qualifies for are determined by its role in Tata Communications' network operations, not by compute density specifications, and those functions are not published here.
